title: Tell a checked exception type from an unchecked one

blocks.text: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared; unchecked ones need not be. Which kind a type is follows from where it sits in the hierarchy. Write `ExceptionKinds.isChecked(Class<? extends Throwable> type)`.

The page names two branches of the hierarchy whose members are all unchecked, and "member" means any descendant, however deep. `Class.isAssignableFrom` answers "is this type that one or a subtype of it?".

cases.says: IOException and SQLException are checked; IllegalArgumentException and NullPointerException are not.
Subclasses of Error are unchecked too, though they are not RuntimeExceptions.
Any descendant of RuntimeException is unchecked, not only its direct subclasses: NumberFormatException is one.

concepts: Checked exceptions are subclasses of Exception but not of RuntimeException, and must be caught or declared.
Unchecked exceptions are RuntimeException and Error and all their subclasses.
